title: Accessible tokens: focus ring improvements, contrast remediation, and ARIA guidance
creator: Ava Kim
description:
Summary: Perform a targeted accessibility sweep focused on semantic design tokens, visible focus states, and ARIA attributes across buttons, data tables, and chart legends. This ticket captures design decisions, token suggestions, and guidance for engineers to remediate contrast and keyboard navigation gaps discovered during the February a11y audit.

Problem statement: Several components render outside of expected contrast ratios and/or lack consistent keyboard focus visuals and ARIA annotation. These issues produce intermittent VPAT failures for ‘Perceivable’ and ‘Operable’ criteria (2.1 and 1.4). We need a design-led remediation plan that is implementable with minimal brand impact and aligns with DS theming patterns.

Scope: primary/secondary/ghost buttons, table row focus/selection states, sortable column headers, chart legend toggles, token mapping (semantic tokens -> color swatches), and a short VPAT artifact update that documents the changes. Not in scope: full component redesigns, new component creation, or wholesale palette overhaul.
acceptance_criteria: All primary/secondary/ghost buttons meet a minimum contrast of 4.5:1 for normal text or 3:1 for large text per WCAG 2.1 AA where applicable
Every interactive control has a visible, 3px minimum focus ring that meets contrast requirements against the adjacent background
Tables: keyboard-only users can traverse rows and activate row-level actions (row focus + aria-selected); sortable columns expose aria-sort and keyboard activation
Charts: legend items are reachable by keyboard and have aria-pressed or equivalent state; color tokens used in charts include accessible fallbacks for high-contrast themes
Design tokens documented in the DS catalog with suggested engineering token names and migration notes
A short VPAT addendum (1 page) describing remediations and residual exceptions is drafted and attached to the PRD
tasks: Audit current token mapping for text and background contrast ratios (run automated contrast tool and hand-check critical combos)
Propose semantic token updates (e.g., token.text.primary-regular -> color that meets 4.5:1 against token.bg.surface)
Design focus ring specs: thickness, color token references, visible offset for outline-less components
Add keyboard mockups for table row navigation and chart legend focus states
Write ARIA guidance snippets for engineers for buttons, sortable headers, and legend toggles
Create a short VPAT addendum with before/after examples and link to test logs
Pair with ENG for an implementation spike and small patch release (include test plan)
Ship token docs and update DS release notes
review_notes: 2026-02-26 — Ava K: initial audit added, automated contrast report attached. Noted primary button contrast 3.9:1 on surface-100 which is below AA. Recommended semantic token path rather than changing raw brand color.
2026-03-02 — PM (Lina Xu): flagged VPAT timeline — legal needs addendum by 2026-03-18 for upcoming enterprise review.

2026-03-04 — Eng (Diego): requested focus ring spec include a no-layout-shift option (box-shadow alternative). We agreed to provide both token-based outline and shadow fallback with implementation notes.

2026-03-08 — Accessibility consultant (Raj Patel): verified proposed button token pair meets 4.5:1 on surface and suggested 3px minimum ring for low-vision users; recommended adding a high-contrast theme test harness.
2026-03-10 — Design review: settled on semantic tokens token.text.on-surface and token.focus.outline with migrations documented in the DS changelog
next_steps: Finalize token mapping doc and publish to DS handbook (owner: Ava)
Coordinate spike with ENG to implement focus ring options and run cross-browser keyboard tests (owner: Diego)
Draft VPAT addendum and circulate to Legal and PM for signoff by 2026-03-18 (owner: Lina)
Create regression test cases for CI (contrast checks and keyboard nav smoke tests) and add to ENG backlog
